subject: Science
central_question: How do curved mirrors and lenses reflect or transmit light to form different images, and how do the laws of reflection explain their behaviour and uses?
in_scope_units: Concave and convex spherical mirrors and their identification.
Image characteristics of plane, concave and convex mirrors and their practical uses.
Incident ray, reflected ray, normal, angles and the two laws of reflection.
Convergence and divergence of parallel light by spherical mirrors and solar concentration.
Convex and concave lenses, their identification and image characteristics.
Convergence and divergence by lenses and uses in optical devices.
banned_topics: Mirror and lens formulae, focal length calculations and ray-diagram case tables.
Detailed refraction laws or refractive-index calculations.
Human-eye defects and optical corrections beyond the examples of lens use.

known_pitfalls.claim: A concave mirror always forms an inverted image.
known_pitfalls.correction: At a small object distance it forms an erect enlarged image; farther away the image becomes inverted and changes size.

known_pitfalls.claim: A convex mirror enlarges nearby objects.
known_pitfalls.correction: It always forms an erect diminished image in the chapter's observations.

known_pitfalls.claim: Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from the mirror surface.
known_pitfalls.correction: Both are measured from the normal at the point of incidence.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only plane mirrors obey the laws of reflection.
known_pitfalls.correction: The laws apply to plane, concave and convex mirrors; curved surfaces change the directions of their local normals.

known_pitfalls.claim: Convex and concave lenses behave like mirrors of the same names.
known_pitfalls.correction: A convex lens converges transmitted light and a concave lens diverges it; a concave mirror converges reflected light and a convex mirror diverges it.
